issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for animal subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat): the problem statement/UML and the solution expect single-argument constructors that accept only the animal name, but the template's commented example in Main.java shows two-argument constructor calls (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")). Specifically, the UML in problem_statement.md declares Animal with a single attribute "name: String" and the solution implements Seal(String), Pig(String), Goat(String). The template's example uses two parameters which will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and may lead to either implementing an extra (unrequired) constructor or leaving the example inconsistent with their code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor usage consistent: update the commented example in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java (template) to use single-argument constructors matching the UML and solution (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if a second attribute was intended, update the UML/problem statement and the solution to include and document the additional constructor parameter and adjust all examples accordingly.

issues.description: Constructor arity/signature mismatch for Animal subclasses: the template's Main.java (commented example) instantiates animals using two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine"), new Pig("Doodle", "domestic"), new Goat("Buttinsky", "mountain")), whereas the exercise specification (UML / problem statement) and the reference solution define single-argument constructors that accept only the animal name (Animal(String name); Seal(String name); Pig(String name); Goat(String name)). A student reading the template example may try to implement two-argument constructors or add a second attribute (e.g., habitat/type), which is inconsistent with the UML and the solution and will cause confusion about the expected class constructors and attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template example with the UML and solution by changing the commented instantiations in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")). If two-argument constructors are actually intended, update the problem statement/UML and the solution implementation to declare and document the second attribute and implement corresponding two-argument constructors consistently.
